headline: Chiefs 24, Dolphins 10
body: Miami hung in it. Down 17-10 into the back half of the fourth, this was a live ballgame until Mahomes found Kelce from 11 yards out and slammed the door. That's the gap between a rebuild and a contender right now: Kansas City closes, Miami doesn't.

Malik Willis played with some fight, 210 through the air and 56 on the ground, and rookie Chris Bell flashed with four grabs for 67. On defense, Jacob Rodriguez was a problem all afternoon, three tackles for loss and an interception. But the drive-killers told the real story: a fumble wiped out a promising possession, and a fourth-and-1 pick snuffed out the last honest shot at a comeback.
Worse than the scoreboard: De'Von Achane went down on Miami's 91-yard opening touchdown drive and never came back, no word yet on how bad. This offense cannot afford to lose its one game-breaker.
Three weeks, three losses. Competitive for three quarters isn't nothing, but it isn't a win either. Minnesota's next, on the road. Time to finish one.
